paper_context.paper_title: Railway viaduct damage and component segmentation benchmark
paper_context.result_scope: numerical segmentation results for synthetic benchmark, conditioning ablation, oracle analysis, real-photo transfer, and zero-shot baseline

experiment_groups.name: Synthetic damage benchmark
experiment_groups.purpose: Compare single-task damage architectures on the synthetic test split

experiment_groups.name: Damage ablation studies
experiment_groups.purpose: Quantify loss, encoder, resolution, and pretraining effects on damage segmentation

experiment_groups.name: Synthetic component benchmark
experiment_groups.purpose: Compare single-task structural/component architectures on the synthetic test split

experiment_groups.name: Joint component-aware conditioning ablation
experiment_groups.purpose: Test whether component-aware conditioning improves damage segmentation

experiment_groups.name: Oracle-filter analysis
experiment_groups.purpose: Check whether the null conditioning result persists on good-component subsets

experiment_groups.name: Synthetic-to-real component transfer
experiment_groups.purpose: Quantify transfer performance on real viaduct photographs

experiment_groups.name: Zero-shot structural GroundedSAM baseline
experiment_groups.purpose: Provide a training-free structural segmentation lower bound on real photographs

primary_metrics.name: foreground mean Intersection-over-Union
primary_metrics.meaning: Primary segmentation accuracy metric excluding dominant background classes

primary_metrics.name: macro Dice coefficient
primary_metrics.meaning: Secondary overlap metric used to support segmentation quality comparisons

primary_metrics.name: frames per second
primary_metrics.meaning: Inference throughput metric used for runtime context

valid_comparisons: Compare synthetic benchmark models within the same task and metric family
Compare joint-conditioning variants using the aggregated summary file only
Compare real-photo transfer and zero-shot baseline only on the real structural/component task
forbidden_comparisons: Do not compare synthetic damage metrics to real structural metrics as if they were the same task
Do not treat prompt-variant GroundedSAM runs as equal-status main baselines
Do not use raw per-run output folders directly when a stable summary CSV exists
aggregation_rules: Use the aggregated means and standard deviations reported in stable CSV summaries when available
Use per-seed rows only when the manuscript explicitly discusses run-level spread or best checkpoints
For real transfer, average the three ConvNeXt rows in results/real_eval_component/real_eval_summary.csv when reporting the manuscript-level mean
comparison_rules.final_run_rule: Prefer the stable table and summary CSVs named in authoritative_files over raw run artifacts and exploratory prompt variants

must_not_report: debug or prompt-search variants as main results
duplicate metrics when one headline metric is already sufficient
interpretation_notes: Keep synthetic damage and real structural results conceptually separate
Treat the paper as a benchmark/null-result paper, not a universal-method-superiority paper
Use only conservative interpretations directly supported by the selected summary files
